readme:
The theme of [temecms.com](https://temecms.com), the TemeCMS project's own website: a product home page, documentation, plugin and theme directories, a migration page, hosting, developers, FAQ, roadmap and a blog.

- Package: `temecms/theme-temecms`
- Theme code: `temecms`
- Licence: MIT

![The home page at 1280 wide](https://temecms.github.io/directory/assets/temecms/theme-temecms/0.3.0/dd2aeb49df6ea216.png)

## Requirements

- TemeCMS `^1.0`

Working on the theme itself (assets, browser checks) needs more: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/temecms/theme-temecms/blob/v0.3.0/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Install

From the admin: open the theme installer, choose to install from a Git address, and give it

```
https://github.com/temecms/theme-temecms
```

Or with Composer, in the Teme install's folder (once the package is on Packagist):

```bash
composer require temecms/theme-temecms
```

Then check it and link its public files:

```bash
php artisan teme:theme:check temecms
php artisan teme:themes:link
```

and activate it under Site › Themes.

To work on a local copy instead, add the theme's folder, as an absolute path, to `TEME_THEME_PATHS` in the Teme install's `.env`. The folder must be named `temecms`, the theme's code.

## What it draws

| Template | Draws |
|---|---|
| `single-page-home` | The home page: opening, four stops, closing |
| `single-page-landing`, `-faq`, `-roadmap`, `single-page` | Pages made of an opening and sections; questions; three columns; plain pages |
| `archive-doc`, `single-doc` | The documentation home (a card per audience, popular pages, what's new) and a guide, in three columns: the tree with the version switcher, the article, "On this page". Search with Ctrl K (⌘ K, or /); code with its language and Copy; Note, Tip and Warning; previous and next; "Was this page helpful?" |
| `archive-plugin`, `single-plugin` | Plugins: search, categories with counts, "Works with Teme", sort, counts, page numbers, and on the first page the strips Recently updated, New and Picked by the Teme team. A plugin's page: its header with Install and Source, the tabs Overview, Screenshots, Changelog, Permissions and Support, and the facts beside them (the review, version, releases, Teme range, categories, package, GitHub, "Ratings and reviews: later", the author with more from them, and Report this listing) |
| `archive-theme`, `single-theme` | Themes, the same as Plugins with picture cards. A theme's page: a gallery in a laptop and a phone frame, Preview before Install, Overview and Changelog, and the facts |
| `archive-showcase` | Showcase: sites built with Teme, by kind, each with its theme and plugins, and the form to add yours |
| `latest`, `single`, `archive`, `search` | The blog, a post, categories and tags, search |
| `notfound`, `error`, `index` | Not found, errors, the fallback |

Page templates an editor can pick: Default, Home, Landing (an opening, then sections), Questions and answers, Roadmap (three columns), and Submit a plugin or theme (the form, the four public steps and the rules in brief).

The directory, Submit and Showcase read the temecms-site plugin's fields (see its README, *The directory*): a listing's summary, icon, categories, latest version, Teme versions, author, links, stars, issues, releases, permissions, screenshots and changelog, and a showcase site's address, kind, screenshot, theme and plugins. The README is the listing's body. A listing's categories are keys; the theme words the directory's own (SEO, Editing, Content and so on) and takes any other from the category's term. The Submit and Showcase forms post to the plugin, which answers back to the page with `?submitted=…` or `?error=…`; the theme's script shows the answer. Without the script every listing shows, unfiltered.

### How a page's content becomes sections

Landing, home, FAQ and roadmap pages split their content at horizontal rules: the first part is the opening, every later part a section. Inside a section:

- a paragraph that is only bold text is the small label above the section's heading;
- an `h2` is the section's heading; `h3` headings followed by paragraphs become cards (two or more make a grid);
- a paragraph that is only a bold link is drawn as a quiet button;
- a numbered list is drawn as steps, and a picture as a picture with its caption.

## Menus

| Slot | Where |
|---|---|
| `primary` | The header |
| `footer-teme`, `footer-build`, `footer-project` | The footer's three columns |
| `docs-editors`, `docs-operators`, `docs-developers` | The documentation's three guides, and the first page of each on the docs home's audience cards |
| `docs` | The documentation's tree: each heading (or item with pages under it) a group. Empty, the tree is the three guides' menus, each of their groups a heading |
| `docs-popular` | The docs home's popular pages |

## Regions

| Region | Where | Cards |
|---|---|---|
| `home-latest` | Home page: from the blog | featured posts (one) |
| `after-content` | After the content of a page or post | callout, button, site code, featured posts |
| `blog-intro` | Blog: opening text | callout, button, image |
| `docs-intro` | Documentation: opening text | callout, button, image |
| `docs-whats-new` | Documentation home: what's new (empty leaves the section out) | callout, button, image |

Fill them under Content › Regions. The regions `plugins-intro`, `plugins-how`, `themes-intro` and `themes-build` are no longer drawn: the directory pages say their own words, as drawn. They stay declared so what they hold isn't lost.

## Settings

Under Site › Themes:

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| Maker line (footer) | Made by Krafty Sprouts Media. |
| The follow link's words | Follow the build |
| The follow link's address (https only) | https://github.com/temecms |
| Status line (foot of every page and the home page; empty shows none) | empty |
| Licence line (empty shows none) | MIT licence |
| Show the latest blog posts on the home page | off |
| Documentation version label (empty shows the Teme release the site runs) | empty |
| Documentation versions, latest first, as `label=address` separated by commas (`1.2=/docs/, 1.1=/docs/1.1/`); with two or more the tree shows a switcher, and an older version's pages a banner | empty |
| The documentation home's address | /docs/ |
| Where "this page didn't help" goes | https://github.com/temecms/teme/issues/new |
| The Plugins page's address | /plugins/ |
| The Themes page's address | /theme-directory/ |
| The Submit page's address (the page with the template Submit a plugin or theme) | /submit/ |
| Writing a plugin, Making a theme, the directory's full rules: their addresses (empty hides the link) | empty |

## The site's content

The theme is only the looks. temecms.com's content types (Documentation, Plugin directory and Theme directory, with their fields), its starting content (pages, posts, guides, listings, pictures, regions and menus) and anything else the site does on its own live in the **temecms-site** plugin, `temecms/temecms-site`, so switching themes never makes content disappear. Install and enable that plugin, then load the content with its seed: its README says how, and how to move a site that the theme's seed (0.1.x) loaded.

The templates for the directories and the documentation keep following the plugin's type keys: `doc`, `plugin` and `theme`.

## Working on the theme

Building the assets, the tests and the browser checks are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/temecms/theme-temecms/blob/v0.3.0/CONTRIBUTING.md). What changed in each version is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/temecms/theme-temecms/blob/v0.3.0/CHANGELOG.md).

## Licence

MIT, copyright Krafty Sprouts Media, LLC. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/temecms/theme-temecms/blob/v0.3.0/LICENSE). The IBM Plex fonts in `public/fonts` are under the SIL Open Font License; see `public/fonts/OFL-ibm-plex.txt`.
changelog:
## 0.3.0

The free plugin and theme directory, as drawn: the theme draws the fields the temecms-site plugin (1.1.0) fills from the directory's index.

- **Plugins** and **Themes** are two pages. Search, categories with their counts, "Works with Teme", sort, the count, equal cards (pictures for themes) and page numbers; on the first page, the strips Recently updated, New and Picked by the Teme team. Without the script every listing shows.
- **A plugin's page**: its header with Install and Source, five tabs (Overview, Screenshots, Changelog, Permissions, Support) and the facts beside them, with "Ratings and reviews: later", more from the author, and Report this listing.
- **A theme's page**: a gallery in a laptop and a phone frame, and Preview before Install.
- **Submit a plugin or theme**, a page template: the form, which the plugin turns into a pull request on the directory, the four public steps and the rules in brief. The plugin's answer shows on the page.
- **Showcase**: sites built with Teme, by kind, each with its theme and plugins, and the form to add a site.
- **The documentation** in three columns: the tree with a version switcher, the article, "On this page". Search with Ctrl K, ⌘ K or /; code with its language and Copy; Note, Tip and Warning; previous and next; "Was this page helpful?". The docs home has a card per audience, popular pages and what's new.
- New settings: the addresses of Plugins, Themes, Submit, the docs home and the guides they link to, the documentation's versions, and where "this page didn't help" goes. New menu slots `docs` and `docs-popular`, and the region `docs-whats-new`.
- The regions `plugins-intro`, `plugins-how`, `themes-intro` and `themes-build` are no longer drawn; they stay declared so what they hold isn't lost.
- The browser checks run light and dark, and `tests/states.mjs` checks the pages' open states (search, preview, tabs, the forms' answers).

Closer to the drawings, everywhere:

- The footer reaches the window's foot on a short page, with no band under it.
- A centred section's heading sits on the page's centre.
- A theme's README pictures: the wide picture stays in the column and the phone picture sits at a phone's size over its lower corner.
- Product pictures on a phone show a version drawn for a phone, and no picture runs past the screen's edge.
- Product pictures are dark in dark mode.
- The footer as drawn: a new setting, The footer's line (words between asterisks in italics), the status line on the left and the licence on the right.
- The phone menu lists FAQ and Roadmap under the header's menu (a new setting, More links in the phone menu), with dividers, a full-width GitHub button, and a cross to close it.
- The Teme icon is the browser tab's icon, light and dark, with a PNG for browsers without SVG icons.
- A code block's name and Copy sit in a bar over the code, and a long line scrolls inside the block.
- Hosting, Developers and Moving from WordPress are laid out as drawn: tables, icons, step cards, code beside its words, the ten places as a grid of five by two, and the usual space between sections.
- A plugin's or theme's Overview leaves out an opening paragraph that repeats the summary in its header.

What a site owner does: update the temecms-site plugin to 1.1.0 and run its directory sync, update this theme, make a page with the template Submit a plugin or theme at `/submit/`, and fill the menu `docs-popular` and the region `docs-whats-new` if you want those sections.

## 0.2.0

The theme is only the looks again. temecms.com's content moved to the new **temecms-site** plugin (`temecms/temecms-site`): the content types Documentation, Plugin directory and Theme directory with their fields, and the seed that loads the pages, posts, guides, listings, pictures, regions, menus and settings. Switching themes no longer takes the site's types with it, and the admin's menu no longer shows Plugins and Themes twice.

- The `seed` folder is gone, and the README and CONTRIBUTING no longer describe seeding; they point to the plugin.
- The documentation pages' version label shows the Teme release the site runs when the Documentation version label setting is empty, which is now its default. With a Teme too old to say its release, an empty setting shows no label.
- The status line's description gives a current example.
- The templates keep their names: they follow the type keys `doc`, `plugin` and `theme`, which the plugin keeps.

What a site owner does: update Teme to 1.2.0, install and enable the temecms-site plugin (it takes over the types the old seed made, with all their content), then update this theme to 0.2.0. Nothing is loaded again. If you once set the Documentation version label, clear it under Site › Themes to show the running release. The plugin's README has the steps, under *Moving an existing site*.

## 0.1.2

- The seed runs on a live Teme install made from the production image. It no longer needs Teme's testing kit or PHPUnit: it acts as the administrator `SEED_ADMIN_ID` itself, and a refused step prints the step and the reason and exits with a non-zero status.
- The seed finds a theme installed from the admin, under the extensions folder.
- The seed's state file is `storage/app/theme-temecms-seed.json` (or `SEED_STATE`), no longer inside the theme's folder, which is read-only on a live site.
- A second run of the seed changes nothing. Regions, menus, menu places, settings, the theme, the theme directory's address and the front page are written only when they differ, and pictures and items an earlier run made are found again without the state file.
- The steps run in one fixed order, the theme before the content, whatever order they are named in. An unknown step name stops the seed before it starts.
- The status line is empty by default, and the footer and the home page leave it out when it is empty.
- The README says how to load the site on a live install; notes for maintainers moved to `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## 0.1.1

- Installs on Teme 1.x: the theme requires Teme `^1.0`.

## 0.1.0

- The theme of temecms.com: the product home page, documentation, plugin and theme directories, a migration page, hosting, developers, FAQ, roadmap and a blog, with the seed that builds the site.
